title: Production Maintenance
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of production maintenance in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to dependency update planning.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers production maintenance within deployment and production readiness. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use production maintenance to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Production Maintenance matters because it is part of deployment and production readiness. In practice, focus on operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.text: Use dependency update planning as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Database migration planning
items.text: Apply database migration planning against a disposable database and synthetic data first. Make transaction ownership and cleanup explicit, parameterize values, and verify constraints and behavior after failures before considering a deployment.

items.title: Zero-downtime deployment concepts
items.text: For zero-downtime deployment concepts, collect measurable evidence from a local or staging environment. Keep configuration environment-specific, avoid logging secrets, establish a rollback path, and do not claim performance or availability without measurements.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Production Maintenance
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open /docs; change the query parameter and observe the injected value.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Dependency update planning”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Production Maintenance”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Dependency update planning” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Production Maintenance, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Production Maintenance belongs to the broader goal of operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
